solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Powdered fruit tablets, first couple taken last, swallowed by champion

indicators.note: something swallowed is taken inside, so the shifted tablets sit within the champion word

parts.note: an ace is a champion, an expert

indicators.note: the opening two letters of the tablets word are moved round to its end

parts.note: pills are tablets

explanation.surface: A recipe step: crushed fruit tablets, rearranged, then gulped down by a sporting champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powdered' belongs to the definition, not an anagram signal: the spice is sold ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The spice is the dried, ground berry of a West Indian tree, sold as a powder.

clue.text: Author off the booze, hiding last three bits of it

indicators.note: the final three letters of the word are concealed, so only the front of it shows

parts.note: it stands for the booze, that is alcohol
TT, teetotal, describes someone who has given up drink

explanation.surface: A writer has sworn off drink, but is hiding some of the stuff away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to 'the booze', ALCOHOL; 'hiding last three bits of' removes HOL, leaving ALCO, followed by TT.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott was the American writer of Little Women.

clue.text: Light coverage of US city politicians duped earliest of electors

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
MPs are Members of Parliament
to have someone is to dupe them, so had means duped

indicators.note: earliest picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A story of politicians in an American city tricking the first voters, given light press coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: MPs are British Members of Parliament; 'had' as in 'you've been had'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade fitted over a lamp covers the light bulb, so it is literally a light covering.

clue.text: Criminal charge overturned and conviction not completed? Sweet!

indicators.note: in a down clue an overturned word is read from the bottom up, so it runs backwards

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in a murder rap

indicators.note: the word is left without its final letter, unfinished

parts.note: faith is a firm conviction or belief

explanation.surface: A criminal charge overturned on appeal and the conviction never completed: sweet result!
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses RAP to PAR; 'not completed' cuts FAITH to FAIT. The legal surface makes 'overturned' and 'conviction' look like court language.
explanation.definitionFit: A parfait is a chilled layered dessert, and dessert is called a sweet in Britain.

clue.text: Check for what kicks off uncivilised youth

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

indicators.note: off means taken away, so that letter is removed from the uncivilised word

parts.note: wild means uncivilised, untamed

indicators.note: what kicks a word off is its opening letter, so this takes the start of the word what

explanation.surface: A warning to check for whatever sets off unruly young people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what kicks off' is W, the first letter of 'what', removed from WILD to leave ILD.
explanation.definitionFit: A child is a young person, so youth in the sense of a young one.

clue.text: Roughly where mother picks up pup to get a snack

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means roughly or approximately
a mother dog carries her pup by the scruff, the back of the neck

explanation.surface: A mother dog roughly grabbing her pup so it can get something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury bite served with drinks, a kind of snack.

clue.text: Nancy's from big country to the north: I must leave with composure

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Nancy is a French city, and the French word for from is de

indicators.note: the letter is told to depart from the country word

parts.note: Russia is the largest country in the world

explanation.surface: Someone from Nancy heading north from a big country, needing to leave calmly.
explanation.walkthrough: RUSSIA loses I ('I must leave') to give RUSSA; DE + RUSSA read 'to the north' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Assured describes someone self-confident and poised, acting with composure.

clue.text: Crooked law's introduction fills in the act

indicators.note: one piece fills a gap inside the other, so it goes within

parts.note: caught at it means caught in the act

indicators.note: a word's introduction is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A crooked law begins by filling in the details of a parliamentary act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at it' means engaged in the act; the L from 'law's introduction' goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tilted at an angle is out of true, skew, so it is crooked.

clue.text: Celebrity turns introducing actual generic sort

indicators.note: the reversed celebrity word takes another word into its middle
the celebrity word turns round and is read backwards

parts.note: a name is a famous person, as in a big name
very can mean actual, as in the very man

explanation.surface: A celebrity turning to introduce someone real, a generic type of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses NAME to EMAN, with VERY placed in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure from the medieval morality play stands for the ordinary, typical person.

clue.text: Distil studies into solid form with a point

indicators.note: one word goes into the other, inside it

parts.note: a cone is a solid shape tapering to a point
dens are studies, private rooms for working

explanation.surface: Instructions to distil what you've studied into something solid and pointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'studies' wants to be CONS; it is DENS, rooms, going into CONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense is to reduce to essentials, much as distilling concentrates a liquid.

clue.text: Micronesian hero adaptable in any circumstances

indicators.note: something adaptable can be changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A hero from Micronesia who copes with whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means whatever the weather, that is, regardless of conditions.

clue.text: Old Arab king behind time with American exhibitionist

indicators.note: the Arab king comes behind, after, the other pieces

parts.note: Ibn Saud was the founding king of Saudi Arabia

explanation.surface: An old Arab monarch lagging behind schedule with an American show-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhibitionist' is not a show-off here but someone who exhibited.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame Tussaud exhibited wax figures, founding the famous London waxworks museum.

clue.text: Cook crumble crust for holiday visitor to Oz

parts.note: to cook the books is to fiddle them, and do can mean swindle in the same way
rot means to decay and crumble

indicators.note: the crust of a word is its outer shell, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A recipe: cook a crumble with a crust for a holiday guest from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oz' suggests Australia, but this is the Land of Oz from The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of The Wizard of Oz is swept by a tornado into that magical land.

clue.text: Keep gasping about the man's divine collection

indicators.note: one phrase goes around the other

parts.note: to pant on is to keep gasping
he is the man

explanation.surface: Breathless amazement at a man's collection of the divine.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is the full set of gods of a religion, a gathering of deities.

clue.text: Labour a long time to dress one glam band up

indicators.note: to dress is to clothe, so the outer word wraps around the rest

parts.note: an eon is an age, a very long time

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
T. Rex was a 1970s glam rock band

explanation.surface: Years of work to dress a glam rock band for the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns I plus the band name into XERTI; T. Rex was Marc Bolan's 1970s British glam rock group.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour and exertion both mean physical effort, hard work.

clue.text: Trouble with old lady's inflexible views

parts.note: to dog is to trouble or plague
an old lady is a mother, ma

explanation.surface: Difficulty dealing with a stubborn elderly woman's opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of principles held as unquestionably true, rigid beliefs.

clue.text: Note interpolated by Flaubert, maybe concerned with taste

indicators.note: something interpolated is inserted into the middle of another thing

parts.note: Gustave is Flaubert's first name, and maybe flags another bearer of it
ti is a note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A note slipped into Flaubert's manuscript, perhaps about matters of taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flaubert' looks like a surname to work with; it gives his forename.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustative means relating to the sense of taste, from Latin gustare.

clue.text: Pace restlessly, crushing rustic seed

indicators.note: the scrambled letters squeeze around the rustic word
moving restlessly means the letters are stirred about

parts.note: a hick is a rustic, a country bumpkin

explanation.surface: Someone pacing restlessly while crushing a country seed underfoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restlessly' rearranges PACE into C and PEA, which surround HICK.
explanation.definitionFit: The garbanzo is the seed of a legume eaten as a pulse.

clue.text: Subgroup of oligarchy enabling predator

indicators.note: a subgroup is a set within a set, so the letters lie inside the words

explanation.surface: A faction within an oligarchy is enabling a predator.
explanation.definitionFit: This African carnivore hunts and scavenges, a predator.

clue.text: Give permission to mobile tool to do roaming

parts.note: an app is a tool on a mobile phone
to rove is to roam

explanation.surface: Allowing a phone app to use roaming abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve is to sanction or authorise, to say yes.

clue.text: Satie mistakenly rounds on downbeat composer

indicators.note: to round something is to go around it, so the shuffled letters enclose the other word
mistakenly set out means put in the wrong order

parts.note: on and leg are both names for the same side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: Satie wrongly turns against a gloomy fellow composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' scrambles the composer's name, split round the inserted piece; in cricket the on side is also called the leg side. 'composer' means a writer of elegies, not music.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegist composes elegies, mournful poems, so a downbeat writer.

clue.text: Sore winner perhaps elected to be annoying

parts.note: a successful candidate is in
to grate is to irritate

explanation.surface: A sulky victor who has been elected and is irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person, like a winner who still complains, is the sort meant.

clue.text: I'm not sure Mass held by boy is what's heard in church

indicators.note: held by means contained within the other word

parts.note: a son is a boy
er is a hesitant noise of uncertainty
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A doubtful boy taking Mass and wondering about what is said in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks religious but it is the physics abbreviation M.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermon is the talk given by a preacher during a service.

clue.text: Pours dry type of wine over sink

indicators.note: turned over means read backwards

parts.note: to tip is to pour
sec is French for dry, describing wine

explanation.surface: Someone pouring a dry wine down the sink.
explanation.walkthrough: TIPS + SEC turned 'over' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cesspit is a pit for sewage, and a sink can mean a place of corruption or a drain.

clue.text: Lack of acceptance underlies small gesture of defiance

indicators.note: in a down clue lying under means coming lower down, after

parts.note: no OK is a refusal to accept

explanation.surface: A refusal behind a little act of defiance.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocking a snook is putting a thumb to the nose, a rude act of defiance.

clue.text: Dance recalled in church with similar origins

indicators.note: one word sits in the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: called back means read backwards

parts.note: the tango is a dance

explanation.surface: A dance remembered in church, from shared roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns TANGO to OGNAT, set in CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognate words or languages share a common ancestor, a related origin.

clue.text: Some knitwear to suit an eccentric?

definitions.meaning: short British word for a cardigan
a card is an eccentric person, so card-like means befitting one

explanation.surface: Knitwear that would suit an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardy is a cardigan, while the playful second reading treats it as card-ish.

clue.text: Reports of shots

parts.note: reports sounds like the bang of gunfire, but here means news stories told through photographs

explanation.surface: Reports of shots
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of journalism tells news stories through photographs, which are shots.

clue.text: Hill-dweller trapping deer pulled back chain

indicators.note: one word traps the other inside it

parts.note: an ant lives in an anthill

indicators.note: pulled back means read backwards

parts.note: an elk is a deer

explanation.surface: A mountain dweller catches a deer and drags it back on a chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hill-dweller' suggests a hill person; it is an ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An anklet is a chain or band worn around the ankle.

clue.text: Cases of pastry rise: nice automation from a range

indicators.note: the cases of words are their outsides, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Pastry cases rise nicely thanks to kitchen automation.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyrenean describes something from the Pyrenees mountain range.
